items.term: Who penned the first issue of The Students Gazette, recognized as the first student publication in the English-speaking world?
items.rationalization: Samuel Fickle Fox wrote the first issue of The Students Gazette on July 11, 1777, on a 4” x 6” sheet of paper at the William Penn Charter School in Philadelphia, USA. It was published continuously until August 1778, when British soldiers closed the school. This makes it the first student publication in the English-speaking world.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: When was the first issue of The Students Gazette published?
items.rationalization: The Students Gazette was first published on July 11, 1777 at the William Penn Charter School in Philadelphia, USA. The date is a high-yield fact because it marks the birth of campus journalism in the English-speaking world.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Where was The Students Gazette, the first student publication in the English-speaking world, published?
items.definition: William Penn Charter School in Philadelphia, USA
items.rationalization: The Students Gazette was published at the William Penn Charter School in Philadelphia, USA. This distinguishes it from Philippine campus journalism, which began much later with UP's College Folio in 1910.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Why did The Students Gazette cease publication in August 1778?
items.rationalization: The Students Gazette stopped publication in August 1778 because British soldiers closed the William Penn Charter School. This historical detail is often tested to check understanding of the publication's brief lifespan.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What was the first student publication in the Philippines, published by the University of the Philippines in October 1910?
items.rationalization: The University of the Philippines started publishing College Folio in October 1910. It printed the works of the first promising Filipino writers in English. This marks the beginning of campus journalism in the Philippines.

mnemonic.title: UP First
mnemonic.phrase: UP's College Folio = First Filipino campus paper

items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In what year did the University of the Philippines begin publishing College Folio?
items.rationalization: College Folio was first published in October 1910 by the University of the Philippines. This is the earliest recorded campus publication in the Philippines.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Which publication did the graduates of Manila High School publish in 1912?
items.rationalization: In 1912, the graduates of Manila High School published their English writings in The Coconut. This is one of the earliest Philippine campus publications after UP's College Folio.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What publication did the Philippine Normal School introduce in 1913?
items.rationalization: In 1913, the Philippine Normal School introduced its publication, The TORCH. It remains one of the oldest continuously published campus papers in the Philippines.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Which literary organ of the UP Writers Club became the most prestigious college literary publication in the country?
items.rationalization: The UP Writers Club, organized in 1927, had its literary organ, The Literary Apprentice, which became the most prestigious college literary publication in the Philippines. This is a high-yield fact about the development of literary campus journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In what year was the UP Writers Club organized?
items.rationalization: The UP Writers Club was organized in 1927 and published The Literary Apprentice, which became the most prestigious college literary publication in the country. Around this time, UST's Varsitarian also began publication.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Which UST publication began around the same time as The Literary Apprentice?
items.rationalization: UST's Varsitarian began publication at about the same time as The Literary Apprentice (late 1920s). Both are among the oldest and most respected campus publications in the Philippines.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: From what Latin word does the word 'journal' come from, meaning 'daily'?
items.rationalization: The word 'journal' comes from the Latin word diurna, which means 'daily.' In ancient Rome, short bulletins of battles, fires, and elections compiled by government officials were posted in public places and were called acta diurna, meaning 'daily events.'
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What were the ancient Roman daily bulletins of battles, fires, and elections called?
items.rationalization: Acta diurna means 'daily events.' These were short bulletins compiled by government officials and posted in public places in ancient Rome. They are considered the earliest precursors of the newspaper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Noah Webster, journalism is defined as:
items.definition: The occupation of writing for publication in newspapers and other periodicals.
items.rationalization: Noah Webster defined journalism as 'the occupation of writing for publication in newspapers and other periodicals.' This is one of the three classic definitions of journalism cited in the BLEPT reviewer.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Who defined journalism as 'something that embraces all forms in which or through which the news and comments on the news reach the public'?
items.rationalization: Fraser F. Bond defined journalism as embracing all forms through which news and comments reach the public. He emphasized that all happenings of public interest, and the thoughts, actions, and ideas they stimulate, become basic materials for the journalist.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the School Paper Advisers of the City Schools of Manila, journalism is:
items.definition: An enjoyable co-curricular activity of the school paper staff in collecting, organizing, and presenting news; in writing editorials, columns, literary articles, and features; in copyreading, proofreading, dummying, and writing headlines – all for the purpose of putting out a school organ.
items.rationalization: This definition by the School Paper Advisers of the City Schools of Manila specifically frames journalism as a co-curricular activity, which is the lens used in campus journalism. It enumerates the full range of staff tasks.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the three areas into which journalism may be divided?
items.rationalization: Journalism may be divided into three areas: written, oral, and visual. Periodicals, brochures, journals, books, and graphic arts fall under print media (written). Radio falls under oral journalism. Television, movies, and documentaries fall under visual journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a publication that comes out at regular intervals – daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, annually, etc.?
items.rationalization: A periodical is broadly defined as a publication that comes out at regular intervals. Newspapers and magazines are the most common examples of periodicals under written journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Compared to a magazine, a newspaper:
items.definition: Prints more news, has no special cover, and is printed on newsprint.
items.rationalization: A newspaper prints more news, has no special cover, and is printed on a special paper called newsprint. News is printed on the front page as well as on the inside and back pages. A magazine, by contrast, prints more features, has a special cover, and is often printed on bookpaper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of paper is a newspaper printed on?
items.rationalization: A newspaper is printed on a special paper called newsprint. This distinguishes it from a magazine, which is often printed on bookpaper and has a special cover.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Compared to a newspaper, a magazine:
items.definition: Prints more features and human interest stories, has a special cover usually with a big cut on it, and is often printed on bookpaper.
items.rationalization: A magazine prints more features and human interest stories, has a special cover usually with a big cut, and is often printed on bookpaper. If news is printed, it is brief, featurized, and found in the inside pages.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Periodicals, brochures, journals, books, and graphic arts are classified under what type of media?
items.rationalization: Periodicals, brochures, journals, books, and graphic arts are classified under print media. Radio falls under oral journalism, while television, movies, and documentaries are under visual journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Radio falls under what type of journalism?
items.rationalization: Radio falls under oral journalism, one of the three areas of journalism (written, oral, visual). Television, movies, and documentaries fall under visual journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Television, movies, and documentaries fall under what type of journalism?
items.rationalization: Television, movies, and documentaries fall under visual journalism. Radio and television are examples of broadcast media, while movies and documentaries are examples of film media.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Radio and television are examples of what type of media?
items.rationalization: Radio and television are examples of broadcast media, while movies and documentaries are examples of film media. This distinction is separate from the written/oral/visual division of journalism.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Movies and documentaries are examples of what type of media?
items.rationalization: Movies and documentaries are examples of film media. Radio and television, by contrast, are examples of broadcast media.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that keeps the public informed of events and issues?
items.rationalization: The information function is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers. It keeps the public informed of events and issues. Other functions include opinion, education, watchdog, laboratory, documentation, entertainment, and developmental functions.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that provides a forum for the expression of views and opinions?
items.rationalization: The opinion function of a campus paper provides a forum for the expression of views and opinions. It is distinct from the information function, which focuses on reporting facts.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that serves as a training ground for future journalists?
items.rationalization: The laboratory function of a campus paper serves as a training ground for students in the communication process. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that monitors and exposes abuses or irregularities?
items.rationalization: The watchdog function of a campus paper monitors and exposes abuses or irregularities. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers and is closely tied to the paper's role as a guardian of public interest.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that preserves records of significant events for future reference?
items.rationalization: The documentation function of a campus paper preserves records of significant events for future reference. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that provides enjoyment and relaxation to readers?
items.rationalization: The entertainment function of a campus paper provides enjoyment and relaxation to readers. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that contributes to national development and social transformation?
items.rationalization: The developmental function of a campus paper contributes to national development and social transformation. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers and aligns with the role of school publications as catalysts for national development.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the function of a campus paper that advances the goals of education and culture?
items.rationalization: The education function of a campus paper advances the goals of education and culture. It is one of the eight functions of modern campus papers.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the engraved or printed name of the newspaper, such as Manila Times or PNC Torch?
items.rationalization: The nameplate is the engraved or printed name of the newspaper, such as Manila Times or PNC Torch. It is one of the elements found on the front page.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the little boxes on either side of the nameplate called?
items.rationalization: Ears are the little boxes on either side of the nameplate. They are one of the front-page elements in a campus paper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the principal headline bearing the boldest and biggest type, serving as the title of the most important news of the day?
items.rationalization: The banner is the principal headline bearing the boldest and biggest type. It is the title of the most important news of the day, called banner news. If it runs across the page, it may also be called a streamer.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a banner headline that runs across the page also called?
items.rationalization: A banner headline that runs across the page may also be called a streamer. The banner is the title of the most important news of the day.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a head made up of two or more lines called?
items.rationalization: A running head is a head made up of two or more lines. It is one of the front-page elements in a campus paper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the title of any news story called?
items.rationalization: The headline is the title of any news story. The word headline is used only for titles of news stories, not for other types of articles.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a subordinate headline placed immediately below its mother headline, also known as bank or readout?
items.rationalization: A deck is a subordinate headline placed immediately below its mother headline. It is also known as bank or readout.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is another name for a deck, a subordinate headline below the mother headline?
items.rationalization: A deck is also known as bank or readout. It is placed immediately below its mother headline.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the beginning of a news story called? It may be a word, a group of words, a sentence, or even a paragraph.
items.rationalization: The lead is the beginning of a news story. It may be a word, a group of words, a sentence, or even a paragraph. It invites the reader into the story and signals the news.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the whole story of an event composed of the lead and the text which is the elaboration of the lead?
items.rationalization: A news story is the whole story of an event composed of the lead and the text, which is the elaboration of the lead. This distinguishes it from just the lead or just the headline.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the horizontal divisions into parts of a newspaper called?
items.rationalization: Columns are the horizontal divisions into parts of a newspaper. Many national papers are divided into eight columns, while a typical school paper is divided into five columns of 12 ems each.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: How many columns does a typical school paper have?
items.rationalization: A typical school paper is divided into five columns of 12 ems each. Many national papers, by contrast, are divided into eight columns.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the vertical line that divides the page into columns?
items.rationalization: The column rule is the vertical line that divides the page into columns. Most pages of a newspaper are divided into columns by a space usually one em wide, called the sunken rule.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the space usually one em wide that divides the page into columns?
items.rationalization: The sunken rule is the space usually one em wide that divides the page into columns. The vertical line itself is called the column rule.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the imaginary horizontal line that divides the newspaper equally into two parts?
items.rationalization: The fold is the imaginary horizontal line that divides the newspaper equally into two parts. Stories placed above the fold are considered more prominent.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the signature of a reporter preceding a news-feature, as 'By Warren Cruz'?
items.rationalization: The byline is the signature of a reporter preceding a news-feature, such as 'By Warren Cruz.' It credits the writer of the story.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are news materials enclosed by line rules called?
items.rationalization: A box refers to news materials enclosed by line rules. It is used to set apart or emphasize certain content on the page.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a metal plate bearing a newspaper's illustration, also known as cliché?
items.rationalization: A cut is a metal plate bearing a newspaper's illustration. It is also known as a cliché. In modern printing, it may refer to any photoengraving.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is another name for a cut, a metal plate bearing a newspaper's illustration?
items.rationalization: A cut is also known as a cliché. It is a metal plate bearing a newspaper's illustration.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the text accompanying photos and other art work, better known as a caption?
items.rationalization: The cutline is the text accompanying photos and other art work. It is better known as a caption. If written above the photo just like a slugline, it is called an overline.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a cutline written above the photo just like a slugline called?
items.rationalization: An overline is a cutline written above the photo, just like a slugline. When placed below the photo, it is simply called a cutline or caption.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a tagline placed above but smaller than a headline, also known as teaser?
items.rationalization: A kicker is a tagline placed above but smaller than a headline. It is also known as a teaser. If it is bigger than the headline, it is called a hammer.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a kicker that is bigger than the headline called?
items.rationalization: A hammer is a kicker that is bigger than the headline. A regular kicker is a tagline placed above but smaller than the headline, also known as a teaser.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a line giving the source of a story or illustration, as 'Reprinted from the Manila Times' or 'Photo by MPI'?
items.rationalization: A credit line is a line giving the source of a story or illustration, such as 'Reprinted from the Manila Times' or 'Photo by MPI.' It acknowledges the origin of the material.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What consists of the page number, date of publication, and name of the newspaper, usually written on top of the page?
items.rationalization: The folio consists of the page number, date of publication, and name of the newspaper, usually written on top of the page. It is also found on the other pages of the newspaper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the editorial box containing the logo, names of staff members and their positions, subscription rate, publisher, and other pertinent data about the newspaper?
items.rationalization: The masthead is the editorial box containing the logo, names of staff members and their positions in the staff, subscription rate, the publisher, and other pertinent data about the newspaper.

mnemonic.title: Masthead = Master Info
mnemonic.phrase: MASTHEAD = Master HEADing of staff info

items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a cut which contains an identifying word or words, such as the name of the newspaper or of a section?
items.rationalization: A logo, short for logotype, is a cut which contains an identifying word or words, such as the name of the newspaper or of a section. It is often found in the masthead.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a commentary written by any of the editors who comments or gives the opinion of the staff or of the whole paper on various subjects?
items.rationalization: The editorial proper is a commentary written by any of the editors who comments or gives the opinion of the staff or of the whole paper on various subjects. It is the stand of the paper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a personal opinion written by the columnist himself or herself?
items.rationalization: An editorial column is a personal opinion written by the columnist himself or herself. Like the editorial proper, it may attack, teach, entertain, or appeal depending upon its purpose.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is usually a caricature emphasizing a simple point, usually humorous, with the function of the editorial?
items.rationalization: An editorial cartoon is usually a caricature emphasizing a simple point. It is usually humorous and has the function of the editorial. It stands by itself and is not a complement of the editorial proper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a short statement or quoted saying placed at the end of an editorial column or editorial to drive home a message?
items.rationalization: An editorial liner is a short statement or quoted saying placed at the end of an editorial column or editorial to drive home a message. It reinforces the editorial's point.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a letter sent in by the reader giving his personal views on certain aspects?
items.rationalization: A letter to the editor is a letter sent in by the reader giving his personal views on certain aspects. It is one of the elements found on the editorial page.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of news takes place within the country?
items.rationalization: Local news is news that takes place within the country. It is one of the types of news found on the front page, alongside foreign news, dateline news, and weather news.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What type of news takes place outside the country?
items.rationalization: Foreign news is news that takes place outside the country. It is one of the types of news found on the front page.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is an out-of-town news story introduced by a dateline stating the place, date, and source of the material?
items.rationalization: Dateline news is an out-of-town news story. It is introduced by a dateline which states the place from which the story was reported, the date, and the source of the material if not written by the local staff, as 'Tokyo, Japan, Jan. 25 (AP).'
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is usually a boxed forecast of the area, sometimes including temperature, wind directions, and velocities?
items.rationalization: Weather news is usually a boxed forecast of the area, sometimes including the temperature, wind directions, and velocities. It is one of the types of news found on the front page.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a slug line indicating an important inside page story and the page where it is found?
items.rationalization: The index is a slug line indicating an important inside page story and the page where it is found. It helps readers locate stories inside the paper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: Sports stories are classified as what type of stories?
items.rationalization: Sports stories are classified as news stories. Therefore, what may be found in the news page may also be found in the sports section. Other things found in the sports section are sports commentaries and sports features.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the two other things that may be found in the sports section aside from news stories?
items.rationalization: Aside from news stories, the sports section may also contain sports commentaries and sports features. Sports stories themselves are classified as news stories.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are examples of special features in a modern newspaper?
items.definition: Society page, Life and Leisure (arts, religion, entertainment, comics), Finance and Business
items.rationalization: The modern newspaper has taken some special features and eliminated others. Examples include the Society page, Life and Leisure (which covers the arts, religion, entertainment, and comics), and Finance and Business.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What may the feature page contain?
items.definition: Home and culture, entertainment, comics, shipping, classified ads, movie, TV and radio guides, and the comics page
items.rationalization: The feature page may contain home and culture, entertainment, comics, shipping, classified ads, movie, TV and radio guides, and the comics page. These are special features of the modern newspaper.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Charter of Student Press Rights, the student press should be free from regulations by any organ of the government or by the university authorities in accordance with what?
items.definition: The right of the United Nations (Draft) Convention on Freedom of Information
items.rationalization: The Charter of Student Press Rights states that the student press, in accordance with the right of the United Nations (Draft) Convention on Freedom of Information, should be free from regulations by any organ of the government or by the university authorities.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Charter of Student Press Rights, the student press should have free access to information and the same rights and privileges as afforded to whom?
items.rationalization: The Charter of Student Press Rights states that the student press should have free access to information and the same rights and privileges as afforded to regularly accredited journalists.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Code of Student Press Ethics, the student journalist should reveal his/her identity as a representative of the student press before doing what?
items.definition: Before obtaining any interview for publication
items.rationalization: The Code of Student Press Ethics states that the student journalist should reveal his/her identity as a representative of the student press before obtaining any interview for publication.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Code of Student Press Ethics, what should the editor do for all mistakes?
items.definition: Apologize in print at the first available opportunity
items.rationalization: The Code of Student Press Ethics states that the editor should apologize in print at the first available opportunity for all mistakes. This upholds accountability and transparency.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Code of Student Press Ethics, the editor should not exclude a student point of view solely because of what?
items.definition: Because it is contrary to the editorial policy
items.rationalization: The Code of Student Press Ethics states that the editor should not exclude a student point of view solely because it is contrary to the editorial policy. This protects freedom of expression within the student press.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Declaration of Principles: Aims of Student Journalists, student journalism must be a means of propagating what?
items.rationalization: The Declaration of Principles states that student journalism must be a means of propagating culture in all its forms. This is the first fundamental principle listed.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Declaration of Principles, what is necessary in order to insure the very existence of journalism?
items.definition: Full freedom of the press exists in the country in which student publications are issued
items.rationalization: The Declaration of Principles states that it is necessary to insure the very existence of journalism that full freedom of the press exists in the country in which student publications are issued, because the freedom of the press exactly reflects the liberty of opinion and expression in any democratic country.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Declaration of Principles, student journalists should pursue and condemn what in all their forms?
items.rationalization: The Declaration of Principles states that student journalists should pursue and condemn totalitarianism, colonialism, and imperialism in all their forms as these are systems opposed to the highest aspirations of students around the world.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to the Declaration of Principles, student journalism declares that it will try to be effective in favor of what?
items.rationalization: The Declaration of Principles states that student journalism, recognizing its responsibility as a medium of expression and orientation, declares that it will try to be effective in favor of student and human rights in accordance with various resolutions of the International Student Press Conference.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the first rule of writing good journalistic style?
items.definition: Cut unnecessary fat. Preserve meaning, but prune ruthlessly.
items.rationalization: The first rule of writing good journalistic style is to cut unnecessary fat. Preserve meaning, but prune ruthlessly. This keeps writing tight and readable.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In writing good journalistic style, what should be chosen over passive voice?
items.rationalization: In writing good journalistic style, choose active over passive voice. Replace 'to be' verbs with action verbs. This makes writing more direct and energetic.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What are the most commonly used transitions in journalistic writing?
items.definition: Chronological (now, since, then, a few days later, etc.)
items.rationalization: The most commonly used transitions in journalistic writing are chronological, such as now, since, then, and a few days later. Crafting transitions carefully is one of the rules of good journalistic style.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: In writing good journalistic style, what should clichés and adjectives be replaced with?
items.definition: Nouns and action verbs focusing on actors and action
items.rationalization: In writing good journalistic style, replace clichés and adjectives with nouns and action verbs focusing on actors and action. This produces more vivid and precise writing.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers see the world as their journalism laboratory, a storehouse of what?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's first trait, good writers see the world as their journalism laboratory, a storehouse of story ideas. If they can get out of the room, they can find a story.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, what do good writers prefer to discover and develop?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's second trait, good writers prefer to discover and develop their own story ideas. They have an eye for the offbeat and may find conventional assignments tedious.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers are voracious collectors of what?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's third trait, good writers are voracious collectors of information. This usually means that they take notes like crazy.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, what is the most important part of a writer's work, the passage that invites the reader into the story and signals the news?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's fourth trait, good writers spend too much time and creative energy working on their leads. They know that the lead is the most important part of their work, the passage that invites the reader into the story and signals the news.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers talk about doing what to the story? They live it, breathe it, and dream it.
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's fifth trait, good writers talk about 'immersing themselves' into the story. They live it, breathe it, and dream it.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, most good writers are 'bleeders' rather than 'speeders.' What does this mean?
items.definition: When they write, they 'open a vein.'
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's sixth trait, most good writers are bleeders rather than speeders. When they write, in the words of sportswriter Red Smith, they 'open a vein.' This means they pour their emotions and effort into their writing.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, what does Saul Pett describe as 'donkey work'?
items.definition: The mechanical drudgery of organizing the material
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's seventh trait, good writers understand that an important part of writing is the mechanical drudgery of organizing the material, what Saul Pett describes as 'donkey work.'
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, what do good writers love because it permits maximum playfulness during revision?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's eighth trait, good writers rewrite. They love computer terminals, which permit maximum playfulness during revision.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, editors 'look for holes in the story' while writers want to do what?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's ninth trait, in judging their work, good writers tend to trust their ears and their feelings more than their eyes. Editors 'look for holes in the story.' Writers want 'to make it sing.'
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers are constantly searching for what side of the news?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's tenth trait, good writers want to tell stories. They are constantly searching for the human side of the news, for voices that enliven the writing.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers write primarily to please themselves but also understand that writing is what between writer and reader?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's eleventh trait, good writers write primarily to please themselves and to meet their own exacting standards, but they also understand that writing is a transaction between writer and reader.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers take chances in their writing and love what kind of approach to a story?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's twelfth trait, good writers take chances in their writing. They love the surprising and unconventional approach to a story.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers are lifelong readers of what, and they also like movies?
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's thirteenth trait, good writers are lifelong readers, mostly novels, and they like movies. They collect story ideas and forms from other genres.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: According to Roy Peter Clark, good writers write too long, and they know it. They want their stories to be 'seamless' or what?
items.definition: Connected by a single thread or to flow
items.rationalization: According to Roy Peter Clark's fourteenth trait, good writers write too long, and they know it. They want their stories to be 'seamless' or 'connected by a single thread' or 'to flow.'
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is the traditional news writing form in which the key points of a story are put in the opening paragraph and the news is stacked in the following paragraphs in order of descending importance?
items.rationalization: The inverted pyramid style is the traditional news writing form in which the key points of a story are put in the opening paragraph and the news is stacked in the following paragraphs in order of descending importance. It allows editors to cut from the bottom without losing essential information.

mnemonic.title: Inverted Pyramid
mnemonic.phrase: Big at top, small at bottom

items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a style of writing in which the major news of a story is reported in the first few paragraphs and then a transitional paragraph introduces a chronology of the events of the story?
items.rationalization: The hourglass style is a style of writing in which the major news of a story is reported in the first few paragraphs and then a transitional paragraph introduces a chronology of the events of the story. It combines the inverted pyramid with narrative structure.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a sidebar to a story?
items.definition: It explores an idea that, while interesting, fails to fit into the main story because it remains tangential to the focus.
items.rationalization: A sidebar to a story explores an idea that, while interesting, fails to fit into the main story because it remains tangential to the focus. Sidebars engage readers by giving more information if they want it, helping to draw them into the issues of the main story.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a news hook?
items.definition: A device that connects the story to current events or timely issues, e.g., 'With only one month to go before the first votes are cast in the Student Government Executive Body elections.'
items.rationalization: A news hook is a device that connects the story to current events or timely issues. The example given is 'With only one month to go before the first votes are cast in the Student Government Executive Body elections.' It draws readers in by showing relevance.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a nut graph?
items.definition: A paragraph that summarizes the essential point or focus of the story, e.g., 'Never before have so many political parties contended so avidly for the votes of the silent majority which definitely will decide the outcome of the elections.'
items.rationalization: A nut graph is a paragraph that summarizes the essential point or focus of the story. The example given is 'Never before have so many political parties contended so avidly for the votes of the silent majority which definitely will decide the outcome of the elections.' It tells readers why the story matters.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper

items.term: What is a cosmic quote?
items.definition: A quote that sums up the story's focus, e.g., 'This is the first time in the local executive body election since the 1980s that four political parties try to mobilize the majority to end their silence and finally speak up,' said Maritess Gomez.
items.rationalization: A cosmic quote is a quote that sums up the story's focus. It often comes from a key figure and encapsulates the significance of the event. The example is Maritess Gomez's statement about the silent majority being mobilized for the first time since the 1980s.
items.tosCompetency: Apply the principles and strategies in writing the various parts of a campus paper
